roman-empire.title: Vexillum of the Roman Empire
desc: - The Roman vexillum was a banner hung from a crossbar, typically red or purple with SPQR and an eagle. It was the precursor to modern flags
- **Construction:** a vexillum (military standard) — a square or vertical banner hung from a crossbar on a pole, typically red or purple with gold embroidered letters 'SPQR' and an eagle motif
trivia:
- Rome had no single national flag — legions used the eagle standard (aquila) but individual units had their own signa
- The aquila (eagle) became the most sacred symbol of Rome, carried into battle
- Loss of the aquila was considered catastrophic dishonour, and recovering lost eagles was a military priority

byzantine.title: Flag of the Byzantine Empire

colors.note: Imperial purple of the Byzantine court.

desc: - The Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire used a gold or purple field with a double-headed eagle, symbolising the empire spanning Europe and Asia
- **Construction:** a red or purple field bearing a gold double-headed eagle. The eagle symbolised the empire's dominion over East and West
trivia:
- The Byzantine Empire (330–1453) was the continuation of the Roman Empire in the East
- The purple colour represented imperial authority and divinity
- The double-headed eagle became the most recognisable Byzantine symbol

holy-roman-empire.title: Banner of the Holy Roman Empire

colors.note: The double-headed eagle of the Emperor.

desc: - The Holy Roman Empire (800–1806) used a gold banner with a black double-headed eagle, representing universal sovereignty over Christendom
- **Construction:** a gold field with a black double-headed eagle bearing a halo around each head. The eagle holds an orb and sceptre
trivia:
- The Holy Roman Empire (800–1806) was a complex political entity in Europe
- The imperial eagle represented imperial authority and religious significance
- Dissolved during the Napoleonic Wars

mongol.title: Banner of the Mongol Empire
desc:
- The Mongol Empire (1206–1368) used the white sulde (spirit banner) with nine horse-hair tails, a sacred symbol representing the spirit of Genghis Khan
- **Construction:** a white field (or sometimes blue) bearing a golden or blue falcon (saker falcon or gerfalcon)
- Mongol standards were often mounted on a pole with horsehair tassels (tugs)
trivia:
- The Mongol Empire (1206–1368) was one of history's largest empires
- The flag represented the vast territorial extent of Mongol rule
- Conquered territories from Europe to the Pacific

achaemenid.title: Standard of the Achaemenid Empire
desc:
- The Achaemenid (Persian) Empire (550–330 BC) used the Derafsh Kaviani, a jewelled royal standard. It was the precursor to the Sassanid standard
- **Construction:** a standard or banner, typically depicting a golden eagle or falcon on a field of purple or crimson
- Achaemenid standards were military vexilloids rather than rectangular flags
trivia:
- The Achaemenid Empire (550–330 BCE) was one of history's largest empires
- Created by Cyrus the Great and conquered territories from Egypt to India
- Known for advanced administration and the Royal Road trade network

kingdom-of-jerusalem.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Jerusalem

colors.note: The silver field representing the Holy City.

desc:
- The Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem (1099–1291) used a white or silver field with a gold Jerusalem cross — unique as it broke the heraldic rule of tincture
- **Construction:** a white (silver) field bearing a gold Jerusalem Cross — a large cross potent surrounded by four smaller Greek crosses
- This is notable as an exception to the heraldic rule against metal-on-metal
trivia:
- The Kingdom of Jerusalem (1099–1291) was a Crusader state in the Levant
- Represented the height of Crusader power in the Holy Land
- Fell to Muslim forces at the end of the Crusades

venice.title: Flag of the Republic of Venice

colors.note: The Lion of St Mark; Venetian maritime power.

desc:
- The Most Serene Republic of Venice (697–1797) flew the Lion of Saint Mark on a red field, one of the most recognisable maritime flags in history
- **Construction:** a red field with the Winged Lion of St Mark holding an open book, typically with a gold border
- The lion is in passant position with its front paw resting on the book
trivia:
- Venice was a powerful medieval and Renaissance city-state and republic
- The winged lion represented Venetian power and maritime dominance
- One of history's greatest trading powers

genoa.title: Flag of the Republic of Genoa

colors.note: The Cross of Saint George; heraldic red of Genoa.

desc:
- The Republic of Genoa (1005–1797) flew a red St George's Cross on a white field, one of the earliest documented maritime ensigns in Europe
- **Construction:** a white field divided into four quadrants by a red Latin cross reaching all edges
- England is recorded as paying Genoa an annual tribute from 1190 onward to fly the same flag under the Republic's protection
trivia:
- Genoa was a dominant medieval maritime republic, rival to Venice, Pisa, and Amalfi
- The St George's Cross remained the flag of the city of Genoa after the Republic fell in 1797
- English ships are said to have adopted the cross because ports along the Mediterranean granted Genoese shipping special protection

seljuk.title: Flag of the Great Seljuk Empire

colors.note: The tamga of the Kınık Oğuz tribe — a black bow drawn with an arrow on its string — forms the emblem.

desc:
- The Great Seljuk Empire (1037–1194) was a Sunni Muslim Turco-Persian empire stretching from Central Asia to Anatolia
- **Construction:** a sky-blue field charged with the tamga of the Kınık tribe — a stylised bow drawn with an arrow on its string — from which the Seljuk dynasty claimed descent
- Note: no single canonical flag survives from the period; this depiction is a modern reconstruction from the Turkish "16 Great Turkic Empires" series, drawing on Seljuk coinage, tamgas, and seals
trivia:
- The Seljuks broke the Byzantine army at Manzikert in 1071, opening Anatolia to Turkic settlement
- The Kınık bow-and-arrow tamga was the clan mark of the Seljuk founders Tuğrul and Çağrı
- The empire fragmented into successor sultanates, including the Sultanate of Rum that preceded the Ottomans

safavid.title: Flag of the Safavid Empire

colors.note: Islamic green; dynastic field of the Safavids.

desc:
- The Safavid Empire (1501–1736) established Twelver Shi'ism as Iran's state religion and flew a green banner bearing the Sun and Lion (Shir-o-Khorshid), a symbol that remained Persia's heraldic emblem into the 20th century
- **Construction:** a plain green field with a golden lion bearing a sun rising behind it; design varied by shah and era
- The emblem fused Zoroastrian solar symbolism with Islamic imagery
trivia:
- Founded by Shah Ismail I at 14; his reign made Iran the only major Shi'a state in the Islamic world
- The capital was moved from Tabriz to Isfahan under Shah Abbas the Great, whose mosques and bazaars still define the city
- The Shir-o-Khorshid emblem was used by Iran until the 1979 revolution

parthian.title: Banner of the Parthian Empire

colors.note: Night sky associated with Mithra worship.

desc:
- The Parthian Empire (247 BC–224 AD) was a Iranian Arsacid state that rivalled Rome in the east; no authenticated flag survives
- **Construction:** modern reconstruction — a black field bearing a large golden sun disc with radiating flame-like rays, drawing on Parthian coinage and the imperial solar cult of Mithra
- The Parthians are better attested by the **Draco** — a wind-sock dragon standard — which later spread to Sasanian, Roman, and steppe armies
trivia:
- Parthian cataphracts and horse archers defeated Crassus at Carrhae in 53 BC, one of Rome's worst military disasters
- The Arsacid dynasty used the title 'Great King of Kings', inherited from the Achaemenids
- Parthian control of the Silk Road made them crucial middlemen between Rome and Han China

delhi-sultanate.title: Flag of the Delhi Sultanate
desc:
- The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) was a succession of five Muslim dynasties — Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi — that ruled much of the Indian subcontinent before the Mughals
- **Construction:** a green field with an off-centre black vertical stripe; this is the depiction in the **Catalan Atlas (1375)** representing the "lord of Delli"
- Different dynasties within the Sultanate used different banners, including plain black (Mamluk) and green with Arabic inscription (later periods)
trivia:
- At its height under the Tughlaqs, the Sultanate briefly controlled most of South Asia
- The Qutub Minar in Delhi was begun by Qutb ud-Din Aibak, founder of the first (Mamluk) dynasty
- The Sultanate collapsed when Babur won at Panipat in 1526, founding the Mughal Empire

maratha.title: Bhagwa Dhwaj of the Maratha Empire
desc:
- The Maratha Empire (1674–1818) flew the **Bhagwa Dhwaj** (saffron banner), a swallowtail pennant long associated with Hindu kingship and Shivaji Maharaj's Hindavi Swarajya
- **Construction:** a plain saffron swallowtail flag — rectangular at the hoist tapering to two points at the fly
- The swallowtail form derives from the Hindu dhvaja tradition; variants with the Raja Mudra (Shivaji's royal seal) were also used
trivia:
- Shivaji Maharaj was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674, formally founding the Maratha kingdom
- At its peak the Maratha Confederacy controlled most of the Indian subcontinent, reducing the Mughals to a nominal presence
- The British East India Company fought three Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775–1818) before finally breaking Maratha power

mali-empire.title: Flag of the Mali Empire

colors.note: The red field as depicted in medieval Catalan atlases.

desc:
- The Mali Empire (c. 1230–1670) was a West African trading empire renowned for its gold and the pilgrimage of Mansa Musa to Mecca in 1324
- **Construction:** a red field with a golden rectangular cantle at centre; reconstructed from the **Catalan Atlas (1375)**, which depicts Mansa Musa seated holding a golden orb beneath this banner
- Note: medieval West African polities did not use national flags in the modern sense; this is a modern vexillological reconstruction based on European cartographic sources
trivia:
- Mansa Musa's Hajj of 1324 distributed so much gold through Cairo that it devalued the Egyptian dinar for a decade
- Timbuktu, under Malian rule, became one of the great centres of Islamic learning with the Sankore Madrasah
- The empire was absorbed by the rising Songhai Empire in the 15th century

teutonic.title: Flag of the Teutonic Order
desc:
- The Teutonic Order (1190–1525) was a German Catholic military order founded during the Third Crusade and later famous for its Baltic Crusades and the state it built in Prussia
- **Construction:** a white swallowtail banner bearing a plain black Latin cross — the order's insignia since its founding in Acre
- The order's black-cross-on-white symbol survives today in the Iron Cross (Prussian/German military decoration) and the Bundeswehr's flag

countryData.name: Teutonic Order
countryData.officialName: Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem

trivia:
- Founded as a hospital brotherhood in Acre in 1190, quickly became militarised
- The State of the Teutonic Order in Prussia (1230–1525) was defeated by Poland–Lithuania at Grunwald in 1410
- The order continues today as a Roman Catholic religious order in Vienna

templar.title: Beauseant of the Knights Templar

colors.note: The upper field — mercy to Christians.

desc:
- The Poor Knights of the Temple (1119–1312) were the first major Christian military order, founded to protect pilgrims to the Holy Land after the First Crusade
- **Construction:** the **Beauseant** — a bipartite banner with black above white — overlaid in some depictions with a red cross pattée
- The Beauseant was the Templars' war standard, reportedly carried into battle with strict rules: knights were forbidden from retreating while it still flew

countryData.name: Knights Templar
countryData.officialName: Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon

trivia:
- The name 'Beauseant' comes from Old French, meaning 'piebald' or 'two-coloured'
- At their height the Templars ran a proto-banking network across Europe, pioneering letters of credit for pilgrims
- Suppressed in 1312 by Philip IV of France and Pope Clement V; Grand Master Jacques de Molay burned at the stake 1314

smom.title: State Flag of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta

colors.note: The Latin cross of the order.

desc:
- The Sovereign Military Order of Malta (1099–present) is the surviving Catholic chivalric successor to the Knights Hospitaller; it is recognised as a sovereign subject of international law without territory
- **Construction:** a red field bearing a plain white Latin cross — the state flag used since the 1960s
- A separate **Order flag** showing the eight-pointed Maltese (Amalfi) Cross on red is used for religious functions
trivia:
- Founded c. 1099 as the Knights Hospitaller of Saint John of Jerusalem to care for pilgrims
- Ruled Rhodes (1310–1522) and Malta (1530–1798) before being expelled by Napoleon
- Today headquartered in Rome on extraterritorial property; issues its own passports, postage, and currency (maintaining diplomatic relations with 110+ states)

lithuania-gd.title: Royal Banner of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania

colors.note: Accents on the knight's harness and sword.

desc:
- The Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1236–1795) was one of medieval Europe's largest states, stretching from the Baltic to the Black Sea at its height
- **Construction:** a red swallowtail banner bearing the **Vytis** ("Chase") — a mounted armoured knight brandishing a sword, the heraldic emblem of the Lithuanian royal house since the 14th century
- The Vytis remains on the modern coat of arms of Lithuania
trivia:
- After personal union with Poland (Krewo, 1386) and formal union (Lublin, 1569), it formed the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
- Grunwald (1410) saw joint Polish-Lithuanian forces crush the Teutonic Order, reshaping Central Europe
- Lithuania was the last pagan state in Europe; Grand Duke Jogaila converted as part of the Polish union

majapahit.title: Naval Flag of the Majapahit Empire

colors.note: Gula — the red half of "Gula Klapa" (sugar and coconut).

desc:
- The Majapahit Empire (1293–1527) was a Hindu-Buddhist thalassocracy based in East Java, whose influence extended across much of today's Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines
- **Construction:** horizontal alternating red and white stripes — known as **Gula Klapa** ("palm sugar and coconut") — recorded as the naval banner of Majapahit fleets
- The same red-and-white dualism inspired the modern Indonesian and Monégasque national flags
trivia:
- Prime Minister Gajah Mada swore the Palapa oath in 1336, vowing to unite the archipelago under Majapahit
- The empire's decline began after the death of Hayam Wuruk in 1389, worsened by the rise of Islamic sultanates
- Majapahit coins and terracotta have been found from the Philippines to Madagascar

khazar.title: Banner of the Khazar Khaganate

colors.note: Turkic blue of the eternal sky.

desc:
- The Khazar Khaganate (c. 650–969) was a Turkic steppe empire centred on the lower Volga, famous for its ruling class's conversion to Judaism and its buffer role between Byzantium, the Caliphate, and the Rus'
- **Construction:** a sky-blue field bearing a stylised wolf standard trailed by five stars — a modern reconstruction from the Turkish "16 Great Turkic Empires" series drawn from Khazar steppe iconography
- No authenticated banner survives; the Khazars used Turkic tamgas and (for their Jewish elite) Hebrew lettering on coins
trivia:
- The Khazar ruling elite converted to Judaism c. 740 — the only medieval state outside Yemen known to have done so
- Khazar power collapsed after Sviatoslav of Kiev sacked their capital Atil c. 969
- Khazarian history survives mainly through the Rus' Primary Chronicle, Arab geographers, and the King Joseph correspondence

sokoto.title: Flag of the Sokoto Caliphate
desc:
- The Sokoto Caliphate (1804–1903) was the largest independent state in 19th-century Africa, spanning much of today's northern Nigeria and beyond
- **Construction:** a plain green field — the banner of Usman dan Fodio's Fulani Jihad and the pan-Islamic green used across the Sahel
- Individual emirates within the Caliphate flew their own variations; plain green is the canonical modern depiction of the Sokoto standard
trivia:
- Founded by the scholar-warrior Usman dan Fodio after his 1804 jihad against the Hausa city-states
- At its height the Caliphate administered some 10 million people across 30 emirates
- Defeated by British forces under Lugard in 1903; its aristocracy was absorbed into the Northern Nigeria Protectorate

kanem-bornu.title: Flag of the Kanem–Bornu Empire
desc:
- The Kanem–Bornu Empire (c. 700–1893) was a long-lived Saharan state of the Lake Chad basin, ruled by the Sayfawa dynasty for over eight centuries
- **Construction:** a horizontal tricolour of blue, yellow, and green — reconstructed from the banner described by 19th-century European travellers to the Bornu court
- The empire merged **Kanem** (north-east of Lake Chad) and **Bornu** (south-west) after Kanem's dynasty relocated following Bulala attacks in the 14th century
trivia:
- One of the longest-lived imperial dynasties in world history — the Sayfawa ruled for roughly 800 years
- An early convert to Islam (c. 1085); Kanem became a major centre of Islamic scholarship in the Sahel
- Final Shehu of Bornu defeated by the Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr in 1893; France absorbed the remnants into its empire
